statement.p: Let f(x) = 8 + 8 \sqrt{x}. Then the expression \frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h} can be written in the form \frac{A}{\left(\sqrt{Bx + Ch} \right) + \left(\sqrt{x} \right)}, where A, B, and C are constants. (Note: It's possible for one or more of these constants to be 0.) Find the constants.
Use your answer from above to find \displaystyle{\lim_{h\rightarrow 0} \frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}}.
Finally, find each of the following:

solution.p: We simplify the expression \frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} = \frac{8+8\sqrt{x+h}-(8+8\sqrt{x})}{h} by multiplying both numerator and denominator by the conjugate and simplifying.
